quote: I do see your your neighbor also has solar, so that's a good sign.
stewart_read: Rep surfaces a genuine social-proof signal (neighbor already has solar) but states it flatly and moves immediately to the roof question without letting it build curiosity or connect to the customer's stated cost-savings motive.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have deliberately kept this brief given the short-call framing set at 00:17, rather than missing an opportunity.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to pause on social-proof lines like this and tie them back to the customer's own stated interest (cost savings) rather than treating them as a checklist item to note and move past.

stewart_read: Customer hands the rep context that explains and potentially inflates his $350/month bill (granddaughter adjusting the thermostat) — a natural anchor point — but the rep responds with a flat acknowledgment and moves straight to the credit qualifier without reflecting the bill context back.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the DQ arrived one question later, the rep may not have had a viable window to build this into a pitch regardless of handling.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to briefly reflect high-usage context back ("so that adds up over the year") before moving on — it costs nothing and reinforces the bill-pain anchor even on calls that may DQ.

quote: You know what? It will be, sir, because, before this divorce I had a a A 760 credit score. And right now, it's set in just about, 625.
stewart_read: This is a second, distinct disclosure — the customer directly ties his credit drop to the divorce, a specific vulnerability trigger. The rep's empathy line arrives at 03:43, several lines later, compressed into the same breath as the DQ notation and the goodbye, rather than as a standalone acknowledgment.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep did include an empathy line ("I'm sorry to hear about that") — this is not a full miss, but a sequencing issue where empathy, DQ-processing, and close all collapsed into one utterance.
coaching_implication: Distinguish this from the 02:11 moment in the 1-on-1: here the rep said the right words but rushed them; the fix is pacing (separate the acknowledgment from the wrap-up), not content.

quote: I'll be looking for you in about six months after I get all this crap she that I inherited from her.
stewart_read: Customer self-schedules a future re-engagement window unprompted. No existing schema section covers converting a self-disqualified customer's stated future-readiness into a logged callback — this is an emergent gap, not a broken rule.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged that formally scheduling six months out was not worth the process overhead versus just notating it for a future list pull.
coaching_implication: This is the single most actionable miss on the call: the customer did the rep's job by naming a callback date. Coach the rep to lock it verbally ("let's put a reminder for six months from now, is [date] fair?") even without a CRM-defined process for it yet — this is a coachable habit, not a script violation.

quote: Thank you. No problem. Bye bye.
stewart_read: The call ends politely but without any next-step artifact — no confirmed callback date, no text promise, no explicit close of the loop despite the customer volunteering timing at 03:36. This is not a violation of button_up (which governs confirmed appointments), but the same closing discipline — locking a concrete next step verbally — would have applied well here too.
alternative_hypothesis: Since this is a hard DQ (credit below 670) rather than a booked appointment, the rep may have correctly judged no formal button-up process applies and treated this as a courteous close, which is procedurally acceptable.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close DQ'd-but-reengageable calls with a stated next action ("I'll reach back out in six months") rather than a plain goodbye — low-cost habit change that turns a dead lead into a pipeline entry.
